items.stem: A support assistant occasionally echoes customers' personal data in its logged responses. Which guardrail capability most directly addresses this?

options.text: PII detection and redaction on inputs and outputs
options.rationale: Correct: redacting PII prevents personal data from appearing in responses and logs.
Model size does not prevent PII exposure.
Removing guidance does not redact personal data.

items.explanation: Correct: redacting PII prevents personal data from appearing in responses and logs.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO statements about evaluating guardrails are sound? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Test against an adversarial red-team set, not only benign inputs
options.rationale: Correct: adversarial tests reveal real bypasses.

options.text: Track both blocked-harmful and wrongly-blocked-benign rates
options.rationale: Correct: both over- and under-blocking matter.

options.text: Assume any configured guardrail is fully effective
options.rationale: Effectiveness must be measured, not assumed.

options.text: Only test inputs the guardrail was designed around
options.rationale: That biases results and misses gaps.

items.explanation: Correct: both keyed options are right; the distractors are wrong for the reasons given.

items.stem: Stakeholders worry a public assistant could answer questions on a prohibited subject. Which guardrail feature fits best?

options.text: Configure a denied topic for that subject
options.rationale: Correct: denied topics block responses on defined subjects.
Token limits do not restrict subject matter.
Model size does not enforce topic policy.
Disabling logging hides activity rather than restricting topics.

items.explanation: Correct: denied topics block responses on defined subjects.
